sourcedFrom: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: Henry's H027 book, and the most detailed teardown the company publishes. The Homesteader is a blowback 9mm carbine that separates into three main components on three receiver cross pins, then gives up its recoil assembly and bolt. The recoil spring is under heavy tension — Henry says so in capitals.

steps.title: Safety on, magazine released and pulled free
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, safety in the ON position with the S showing. Press the magazine release on the centre front face of the magazine well and pull the magazine out. The release sits on the front of the well rather than behind the trigger guard, so reach forward for it — and take the magazine out before touching the bolt, because a loaded magazine will just feed another round.
steps.quote: press the magazine release on the center front of the magazine well, then pull the magazine free.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY HOMESTEADER 9MM CARBINE, step 1, p.16
steps.warn: ALWAYS ASSUME THE CHAMBER IS LOADED, EVEN AFTER REMOVING THE MAGAZINE FROM THE RECEIVER.

steps.title: Bolt back and locked open on the bolt catch
steps.action: Pull the bolt fully to the rear and press the bolt catch lever to hold it open. If a round was chambered it is ejected now, which is the point of doing it after the magazine came out. Let the charging handle travel its full stroke — a short pull may extract without throwing the case clear of the port.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt fully to the rear and press the bolt catch lever to hold the bolt open. This will eject an unfired round from the chamber if the magazine was not empty.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY HOMESTEADER 9MM CARBINE, step 2, p.16

steps.title: Chamber inspected by eye through the open port
steps.action: With the bolt locked back, look into the ejection port on the right side and confirm the chamber is empty before the carbine is cased, stored or worked on. Do this by sight, not by feel and not by trusting the previous two steps — this is the check that catches the round that did not eject cleanly.
steps.quote: Visually inspect the chamber to verify the firearms unloaded condition prior to casing or storing.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY HOMESTEADER 9MM CARBINE, step 3, p.16

steps.title: Henry's stated precondition for taking it apart
steps.action: Henry sets an explicit condition before any disassembly begins: magazine out of the well AND the action locked open on the bolt stop lever. Both, and in that order. It is printed at the head of the cleaning section rather than buried in the disassembly text, which is where people start reading.
steps.quote: THE MAGAZINE SHOULD BE REMOVED FROM THE MAGAZINE WELL AND ACTION LOCKED OPEN USING THE BOLT STOP LEVER AS DESCRIBED ON PAGE 15 BEFORE ATTEMPTING DISASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — CLEANING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, p.19

steps.title: Eye protection on before any spring comes under your hands
steps.action: Put safety glasses on before you start. Henry gives the reason plainly: components in this carbine are under spring tension, and the recoil assembly in particular is held compressed by hand during the strip. Verify the unloaded condition once more as you begin — the book asks for it here too.
steps.quote: Safety glasses should be warn as many components are under spring tension. Be sure to verify the firearms unloaded condition before proceeding.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.20

steps.title: Three receiver cross pins driven out with a 1/8 inch roll pin punch
steps.action: Drive the three receiver cross pins out with a 1/8 inch roll pin punch — a roll pin punch specifically, because its tipped face will not skate off and mark the anodised receiver the way a flat drift does. The three pins are what hold the carbine's three main components together. Support the receiver on a block rather than driving against thin air.
steps.quote: The gun can be taken down into three main components by driving the three receiver cross pins (Part # H27-88) out with a 1/8” roll pin punch.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Trigger group and buttstock slid out, magazine well rocked free
steps.action: Hold the forearm in one hand and the stock in the other and slide the trigger group and buttstock out of the receiver groove, pressing down on the top of the stock wrist as you go. The magazine well then comes away after rocking it back and forth. It is a sliding groove joint, not a hinge — if it resists, a pin is still in, not more force.
steps.aside: You'll now have the gun broken down into three components and since the receiver holds the most fouling, further disassembly is generally not required.
steps.quote: The magazine well comes free after rocking back/forth.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Forearm screw out, forearm slid forward off the receiver slot
steps.action: Undo the forearm screw with a 1/8 inch hex key and slide the forearm forward and out of the receiver slot. Forward, not down — it disengages along the slot. This has to happen before the recoil assembly can be reached, and it is the step that exposes the guide rod and weight you are about to hold under tension.
steps.quote: Unscrew the forearm screw (1/8”), then slide the forearm forward and out of the receiver slot.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: Recoil spring taken under control before anything is released
steps.action: Stop and read this before touching the recoil assembly. The spring is under heavy tension and Henry requires it to be held tight while the rod and weight come out. This is the step that fires parts across a room. Get a firm grip established first, then work — do not start the operation one-handed and improvise.
steps.quote: WARNING: THE RECOIL SPRING IS UNDER HEAVY TENSION AND SHOULD BE HELD TIGHT WHILE REMOVING THE ROD AND WEIGHT.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.21
steps.warn: THE RECOIL SPRING IS UNDER HEAVY TENSION AND SHOULD BE HELD TIGHT WHILE REMOVING THE ROD AND WEIGHT.

steps.title: Guide rod pinched, weight pushed back, action bar tabs peeled off
steps.action: Pinch and hold the guide rod ahead of the weight between left thumb and index finger, then push back on the weight until the front tabs of the action bars can be peeled off it. Pop the rear tabs out of the bolt and take the bars out. The pinch on the rod ahead of the weight is what stops the spring escaping — keep it until both bars are off and the weight is back under control.
steps.caution: The action bars are left- and right-hand specific; keep track of which came off which side.
steps.quote: With the left hand, thumb and index finger, pinch and hold the guide rod ahead of the weight, then push back on the weight until the front tabs of the action bars can be peeled away from the weight. Now pop the rear action bar tabs out of the bolt and remove them.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: Charging handle out, bolt removed
steps.action: Pull the charging handle straight out of the bolt slot and lift the bolt out for cleaning. The handle is retained by the bolt rather than screwed in, which is also why it can be swapped to the other side of the receiver. That is the strip complete: the receiver holds most of the fouling and Henry says nothing beyond this is normally needed.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle out and remove the bolt for cleaning.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Receiver, trigger group with buttstock, magazine well, forearm, recoil rod and weight, action bars, bolt and charging handle are now separate. That is Henry's published strip for the Homesteader. The Deep Clean branch covers the hammer/trigger group, the magazines and the wood, all of which the manual treats separately.
steps.quote: If the bore has already been cleaned with the gun assembled and bolt held open, spray, brush and patch the bolt and inner receiver clean where accumulated fouling is seen. Dry, then coat all metal surfaces with a thin film of good quality light gun oil.
steps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

deepSteps.title: Hammer and trigger group sprayed and brushed — and left assembled
deepSteps.action: With the trigger group out of the receiver it can be sprayed and brushed clean as a unit. Leave it as a unit: Henry states the trigger is non-adjustable and that further disassembly of that assembly should not be attempted. There is nothing to set and nothing to gain, and the fire-control parts are the ones you cannot buy back on a Sunday.
deepSteps.quote: The Hammer/trigger group can now be sprayed and brushed clean. The trigger is non-adjustable and further disassembly of that assembly should not be attempted.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

deepSteps.title: Magazine body and follower brushed with a plastic-safe solvent
deepSteps.action: Brush the follower clean and use a plastic-safe solvent on it and on the magazine body — plastic-safe matters, because an aggressive bore solvent will craze the polymer follower. Check the feed lips for damage while it is in your hand and make sure the follower still runs up and down freely; a sticky follower is a failure to feed waiting to happen.
deepSteps.prose: Be sure to check for any damage to feed lips and verify the followers ability to move up and down freely.
deepSteps.quote: Routine maintenance consists of brushing the follower clean and using a plastic safe solvent to clean it and the magazine body.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — MAGAZINES, p.20

deepSteps.title: Magazine floor plate off for access to the spring
deepSteps.action: Push the button on the base of the magazine and slide the floor plate forward to open it up, which gives access to the spring and the underside of the follower. Keep a thumb over the plate as it slides — there is a spring behind it. Clean, dry and reassemble; do not oil the inside of a magazine, as oil there collects powder and makes feeding worse.
deepSteps.quote: The floor plate can also be removed by pushing the button on the base and sliding forward.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — MAGAZINES, p.20

deepSteps.title: Bore cleaned in the direction of bullet travel
deepSteps.action: Clean the bore following the bullet, from breech toward the muzzle. Henry warns that going muzzle-to-breech carries powder residue back out of the bore into the chamber and action, where it fouls the intricate parts. With the bolt out you have a clear path in from the rear, so on this carbine there is no excuse to do it the other way.
deepSteps.quote: WHENEVER POSSIBLE, CLEAN THE BORE IN THE DIRECTION OF BULLET TRAVEL.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.21

deepSteps.title: Walnut stock: sealed finish, very little wanted
deepSteps.action: The American Walnut stocks are sealed with a satin polyurethane finish, so the wood needs almost nothing — a wipe with a soft cloth. Do not feed oil into a sealed finish; it has nowhere to go and will sit on the surface. Keep gun oil off the wood generally, and wipe any that has run down from the action.
deepSteps.quote: The wood pores of this model's American Walnut stocks are sealed with a satin polyurethane finish and require little maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — WOOD CARE, p.21

deepSteps.title: Rebuild: bolt and charging handle, then the action bars one side at a time
deepSteps.action: Put the bolt back in and re-insert the charging handle. Then fit the action bars one side at a time — rear tabs into their bolt slots first, then push the weight back against the spring to get the front tab on, and let it out slowly so the tab slides home. The bars are left- and right-hand specific, so a bar that will not seat is probably on the wrong side.
deepSteps.prose: Replace the bolt and re-insert the charging handle.
deepSteps.quote: Fit the right side bar (left and right specific) rear tabs into their bolt slots. Push back on the weight against the spring to fit the front tab to the weight. When slowly released, the front tab will slide home. Repeat for the left hand side.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — REASSEMBLY, p.22

deepSteps.title: Magazine well seated, halves slid together, three pins back in
deepSteps.action: Fit the front tab of the magazine well into the receiver slot and push forward until it seats, then line the receiver and trigger guard grooves up and slide the two halves back together. The three cross pins go back from either direction. The pins should push in against light resistance — if one needs driving hard, the grooves are not fully aligned.
deepSteps.quote: Fit the front tab of the magazine well into the receiver slot and push forward until seated. Align the receiver and trigger guard grooves to slide the two halves back together. Replace the receiver pins from either direction.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H027 Homesteader 9mm User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — REASSEMBLY, p.22

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: With the bolt out, clean the bore from the breech toward the muzzle
Fresh patch face each pass until clean, then dry and lightly oil
Wipe the chamber and the feed ramp at the barrel breech

cleaning.name: BOLT, RECEIVER & ACTION BARS
tasks: Spray, brush and patch the bolt and inner receiver where fouling has built up
Wipe the action bars and the guide rod and weight
Dry everything, then a thin film of good quality light gun oil on the metal

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES & FURNITURE
tasks: Brush the follower and body with a plastic-safe solvent only
Check feed lips for damage and the follower for free movement
Wipe the sealed walnut with a soft cloth; keep gun oil off the wood

reassembly: Replace the bolt and re-insert the charging handle.
Fit each action bar rear tabs first, then the front tab onto the weight, releasing it slowly.
Attach the forearm and start the forearm screw by hand.
Seat the magazine well front tab into the receiver slot and push forward until seated.
Align the receiver and trigger guard grooves, slide the halves together and replace the three receiver pins.
fncheck: With the carbine confirmed empty and no magazine fitted, pull the charging handle fully to the rear and let it run forward under spring force — it must travel freely and close fully. Check the bolt catch holds the bolt open and releases, confirm the safety moves between ON and OFF, and confirm an empty magazine seats and releases before loading.
